title: Happiest Minds Technologies Ltd - 543227 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Happiest Minds FY26 revenue rose 12.3% in INR to INR2,315 crore (9.2% constant currency) and FY27 guidance of 12.5% CC growth was reconfirmed.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 operating revenue was INR604 crore, up 2.8% QoQ and about 11% YoY, with constant-currency growth of only 0.5% QoQ and 6.4% YoY. Management attributed the soft quarter mainly to right-shifted Arttha licence deals and a pause in a large Hi-Tech customer's new product engagement. Full-year constant-currency growth of 9.2% was below the 10% guidance. Management reconfirmed FY27 CC growth guidance of 12.5%, says it is built on a 15% revenue plan, and guides operating margin up about 100 bps to 17.5-18.5% (explicitly not called guidance).

financial_highlights.change: up vs previous year and previous quarter; includes exceptional items
vs 17.3% in FY25; INR401 crore up 12.3%

financial_highlights.value: ~81% in Q4 (vs 77.4% a year ago); above 81% for FY26 (vs 77%)

segments.name: GBS (Generative AI Business Services)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 3.3% of revenue with about 200 dedicated people; management says it is an innovation centre, not a profit-centre, and its margin decline QoQ was questioned. Profitability is captured in PDES and IMSS.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Led FY26 growth alongside Healthcare; management says PureSoftware and Aureus acquisitions are paying off, with strong QoQ and YoY growth.

segments.name: Healthcare and Life Sciences
segments.commentary: Grew 12.8% YoY but dipped 5% QoQ in Q4 because a pharma licence revenue element completed in Q3.

segments.name: Hi-Tech
segments.commentary: Sharp QoQ decline in Q3 and Q4 attributed mainly to one Canada/China-linked customer pausing a new AI-driven automated cooking product after completion.

segments.name: EdTech
segments.commentary: Grew 8.4% QoQ in Q4; Eduweave platform has a couple of customers and several prospects; traction returning in previously challenged accounts.

segments.name: Retail, Travel, Media and Entertainment, Industrial
segments.commentary: Retail/CPG and travel/media delivered steady growth; industrial stable. Retail and CPG cited as having good traction.

guidance_outlook: FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance of 12.5% reconfirmed by the Board; management is aspirational about 15%. Revenue plan built for 15%, P&L built on 12.5%.
FY27 operating margin to improve about 100 bps to 17.5-18.5%; management says it is not formal guidance and will be achieved while funding AI investment.
FY27 planned headcount of 1,050, with most hiring in the GBS unit and the analytics and AI CoE.
Management will target 90%+ of engineers, testers and service delivery staff trained on and using AI productivity tools by end FY27.
Plans to build a dedicated 1,000-person AI and generative AI team by end FY27.
Will report AI-led services revenue and pricing models (AI-first vs T&M/fixed price) in coming months. Right-shifted Arttha deals targeted to close in Q1 FY27.
FY27 guidance is organic only; any acquisition would be on top of it, and no acquisition is in the pipeline.
capex_capacity: Planned FY27 headcount of 1,050; FY26 ended with about 6,500 people, a slight drop YoY, and attrition of 17%.
Utilisation about 81% in Q4 and above 81% for FY26, up from about 77%.

Enterprise AI platform launched recently; Relay Build (agentic SDLC tool, 40% adoption across internal and customer projects) and Agent Hub (guardrails for coding agents) are AI productivity platforms.
Sales headcount to increase in FY27 as open positions filled; hybrid BDMs shifting to client partners and account managers.
New partnerships: Anthropic (early partner, formalised Q4) and UnifyApps (360-degree partnership), in addition to existing Microsoft and AWS ties.
demand_pricing: Q4 pipeline grew 27% QoQ (record), a mix of new and existing business.
Repeat business about 92-94% of revenue; billion-dollar clients rose from 82 to 91 and contribute about 58% of revenue.
FY26 added 51 active customers to reach 306.

Named wins include a US insurance and financial services provider (product engineering), a global warehouse automation leader (engineering and security), and a European healthcare software company (hospital management modernisation).
Warehouse and logistics take-over deal: 3-year, about $12-15 million; a further engineering deal in discussion at about $8-10 million over 3 years.
Southeast Asia insurer account at $10 million-plus, grown 40% YoY with two large new programmes.
Preferred partner for 4 private equity firms, a source of pipeline. Two new BUs under large-account leaders; aim to create 1-2 $20 million accounts in FY27.
Management declined to give TCV/ACV, citing no industry-standard formula; says it is working on it.
Pricing shifting toward outcome-based models as AI changes service offerings.

qa_highlights.question: Beyond the Arttha right-shift, what caused softer Q4 growth, notably the sharp QoQ drop in Hi-Tech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management tied the Hi-Tech drop largely to one Canada/China-linked customer pausing a newly built AI-driven cooking-hardware product after completion. Healthcare fell 5% QoQ in Q4 after a pharma licence revenue element completed in Q3; EdTech grew 8.4% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the GBS segment margin decline QoQ, and which AI platforms have adoption metrics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GBS is an innovation centre with no separate profitability target; its profit shows up in PDES and IMSS. Relay Build has 40% adoption across internal and customer projects. ELAIRA is an AI companion to ELLIPSE, and SecAIGenie, Eduweave and Insurance-in-a-box are other platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 12.5% FY27 guidance is covered by won deals versus pipeline conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix. Plans were built bottom-up by industry groups, IMSS, GBS and CoEs, and stress-tested for H1. The P&L is built on 12.5% against a 15% revenue plan. Repeat business is 92-94%, and multi-year deals give some cushion.

qa_highlights.question: Will sales and AI investments rise in FY27, and what are the margin headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales cost will rise somewhat as open positions are filled and the hybrid BDM model shifts to client partners. AI investment continues. Management says these are not headwinds per se and that margin is still targeted at 17.5-18.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in FY27 revenue acceleration, and which verticals will lead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the pipeline, the 92-94% repeat base, large multi-year deals, PE partnerships, and new large-account BUs under Rohit Mathur (Hi-Tech, industrial, EdTech) and Prathamesh Kulkarni (retail CPG, BFSI, healthcare). It declined to give TCV/ACV for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is any of the 12.5% inorganic, and how is the company different from platform players in AI?
qa_highlights.answer: The 12.5% is entirely organic; acquisitions are integrated and no acquisition is in the pipeline. On differentiation, management cited its separate GBS unit, repeatable solutions, an SDLC CoE for AI productivity tools, and a deliberate delay in building a broad platform until experience was gained.

qa_highlights.question: Succession planning, given promoter holding of about 32%.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said succession planning has been an annual Board-reviewed exercise since 2012, with Hogan assessments added last year, IIM Bangalore and ISB programmes, and some leaders hired externally.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 must close the right-shifted Arttha licence deals to support the 12.5% guidance.
Hi-Tech customer pause could affect revenue if the product launch stalls.
DSO rose to 94 days from 92; management expects recovery via post-quarter collections.
Attrition at 17% and headcount falling to about 6,500 in FY26 against planned 1,050 FY27 hiring.
Margin expansion of about 100 bps depends on utilisation, integration efficiencies and currency, with forward-contract losses noted.
Management has not disclosed TCV/ACV, and the AI-led revenue and AI pricing-model disclosures are still pending.
Sales-team transition and GBS profitability reporting are open questions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium term and the FY27 plan, but more cautious on the quarter, where it explained the miss with specific accounts. It was evasive when pressed on GBS margin and on TCV/ACV, deferring both.
key_quotes: We're putting all our energy and focus into meeting our guided growth of 12.5% in constant currency for the next year.
Efforts are underway to close these right-shifted deals in the first quarter of the current year.
And we've built the plan for 15%, whereas we've kind of -- the revenue plan, but the P&L has been built on 12.5%.
So we don't look at this as really being headwinds. It could be transitory.
Happiest Minds is the only company that has a separate business unit for generative AI.
But at our size of 300 million, it's all about focused execution on the current pipeline and the opportunities, Dipesh.

growth.why: FY27 CC growth guidance of 12.5% was reconfirmed, with a 15% revenue plan behind it; backing is partial (record Q4 pipeline up 27% QoQ, $10M+ and billion-dollar client wins, 1,050 planned hires, AI team build), but no new capacity or contracted order book was quantified, and FY26 CC growth missed the 10% guide at 9.2%.
